contentBlocks.text: ਤੁਸੀਂ ਪਰਿਵਾਰ ਬਾਰੇ ਲਿਖਿਆ। (You've written about family.) Today, let's write about something just as personal: your own daily routine.

Three new words: ਸਵੇਰ (savera, morning), ਦਿਨ (din, day), and ਜਾਣਾ (jana, to go — the same verb pattern you know, with forms ਜਾਂਦਾ/ਜਾਂਦੀ for 'goes'). Try this sentence pattern: ਸਵੇਰੇ, ਮੈਂ ਸਕੂਲ ਜਾਂਦਾ/ਜਾਂਦੀ ਹਾਂ। (In the morning, I go to school.) Write 2-3 sentences describing your own morning routine, using ਸਵੇਰ and ਜਾਣਾ.
You just wrote real sentences describing your own daily life in Punjabi. Tomorrow we'll write about a favorite family tradition or celebration.

objectives: Learn 3 new vocabulary words: ਸਵੇਰ, ਦਿਨ, ਜਾਣਾ
Write 2-3 sentences describing a personal daily routine using the new vocabulary
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review this week's family vocabulary so far.
2. Introduce today's 3 new words and the example sentence pattern.
3. Have the child write their own morning-routine sentences, choosing the correct masculine/feminine verb form.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's topic: family traditions and celebrations.
differentiationTips: Struggling: provide the sentence pattern as a fill-in-the-blank rather than requiring the child to construct it from scratch
Ready for more: ask them to add a second sentence about what they do after school, using ਦਿਨ
All Gurmukhi words/sentences used in this lesson were validated against gurmukhifix's Lexicon before writing
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1. ਸਵੇਰ = morning. 2. ਦਿਨ = day. 3. ਜਾਣਾ = to go. Sample sentence: ਸਵੇਰੇ, ਮੈਂ ਸਕੂਲ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹਾਂ। = In the morning, I go to school.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Continues the course's 'paragraph writing' and 'vocabulary expansion' goals with a personally meaningful writing topic (daily routine), building sentence-construction skill toward Day 5's full-paragraph synthesis.
